questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The commonest direct cause of maternal death in India is:
questions.concept: Postpartum haemorrhage is the leading direct cause of maternal death in India, followed by sepsis, hypertensive disorders and unsafe abortion. Anaemia is the most important indirect contributory cause.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The maternal mortality ratio is expressed as maternal deaths per:
questions.concept: The maternal mortality ratio uses 100,000 live births as the denominator and counts deaths during pregnancy or within 42 days of termination from causes related to pregnancy, excluding accidental causes.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The analgesic technique of choice for labour is:
questions.concept: Continuous lumbar epidural gives the most effective pain relief with an awake mother, and is particularly valuable in cardiac disease and pre-eclampsia. It may modestly prolong the second stage and increase instrumental delivery.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The preferred anaesthetic for an elective caesarean section is:
questions.concept: Regional anaesthesia avoids the risks of failed intubation and aspiration, keeps the mother awake and gives better neonatal outcomes, so spinal block is standard. General anaesthesia is reserved for extreme urgency or contraindications to regional block.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Mendelson syndrome refers to:
options: Chemical aspiration pneumonitis from gastric contents during obstetric anaesthesia
questions.concept: Aspiration of acidic gastric contents causes severe chemical pneumonitis with bronchospasm and hypoxia. Pregnant women are at high risk from a lax cardiac sphincter and delayed emptying, so fasting, antacids, H2 blockers and cricoid pressure are used.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Supine hypotension syndrome in late pregnancy is caused by:
options: Compression of the inferior vena cava by the gravid uterus reducing venous return
questions.concept: In the supine position the gravid uterus compresses the inferior vena cava, reducing venous return, cardiac output and uterine perfusion, causing hypotension. Left lateral tilt relieves it and is routine during anaesthesia.
questions.reference: Ganong Review of Medical Physiology; Williams Obstetrics 26e

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The most important single intervention to reduce maternal mortality from haemorrhage at the community level is:
options: Institutional delivery by a skilled birth attendant with referral linkage
questions.concept: Skilled attendance at birth with active third-stage management and functioning referral for emergency obstetric care is the cornerstone, supported by schemes such as Janani Suraksha Yojana and Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Amniotic fluid embolism classically presents with:
options: Sudden hypoxia, cardiovascular collapse and disseminated intravascular coagulation
questions.concept: Amniotic fluid embolism causes abrupt hypoxia, hypotension and consumptive coagulopathy, often during or immediately after labour, with very high mortality. Management is supportive with aggressive resuscitation and blood product replacement.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: A near-miss maternal case is defined as a woman who:
options: Survived a life-threatening complication during pregnancy, childbirth or within 42 days of termination
questions.concept: Reviewing near-miss cases identifies gaps in care with far greater numbers than maternal deaths alone, making audit statistically useful and less blame-oriented; WHO defines it by organ-dysfunction criteria.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Pudendal nerve block is most useful for:
options: Perineal analgesia for instrumental delivery and episiotomy repair
questions.concept: The pudendal nerve carries somatic sensation from the perineum, so blocking it at the ischial spine relieves perineal pain for outlet forceps, vacuum and episiotomy, but does not relieve uterine contraction pain of the first stage.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Genital infections, PID & STIs in women
questions.stem: The commonest cause of vaginal discharge with a fishy odour and clue cells on microscopy is:
questions.concept: Bacterial vaginosis results from replacement of lactobacilli by Gardnerella and anaerobes, giving thin grey discharge, pH above 4.5, a positive whiff test and clue cells. Amsel criteria require three of four features; treatment is metronidazole.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Vaginal Discharge

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Genital infections, PID & STIs in women
questions.stem: A strawberry cervix with profuse frothy greenish discharge indicates:
questions.concept: Trichomoniasis causes frothy offensive discharge with vulvovaginal itching and punctate cervical haemorrhages (strawberry cervix), with motile flagellates on wet mount. Both partners are treated with metronidazole.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Vaginal Discharge

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Genital infections, PID & STIs in women
questions.stem: Thick white curdy discharge with intense pruritus and pseudohyphae on KOH mount indicates:
questions.concept: Candidal vaginitis gives adherent curdy plaques with vulval erythema and a normal vaginal pH below 4.5, and is common in diabetes, pregnancy, antibiotic use and immunosuppression. Topical or oral azoles are used.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Vaginal Discharge

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Genital infections, PID & STIs in women
questions.stem: The most serious long-term consequence of pelvic inflammatory disease is:
options: Tubal infertility and ectopic pregnancy from tubal damage
questions.concept: Each episode of pelvic inflammatory disease roughly doubles the risk of tubal infertility and increases ectopic pregnancy risk six to ten-fold, along with chronic pelvic pain from adhesions - hence the emphasis on early empirical treatment.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Genital infections, PID & STIs in women
questions.stem: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome refers to:
options: Perihepatitis with violin-string adhesions complicating chlamydial or gonococcal PID
questions.concept: Transperitoneal spread of Chlamydia or gonococcus to the liver capsule causes perihepatitis with right upper quadrant pain and characteristic violin-string adhesions seen at laparoscopy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Genital infections, PID & STIs in women
questions.stem: Empirical treatment of outpatient pelvic inflammatory disease should cover:
questions.concept: Standard regimens combine ceftriaxone for gonococcus with doxycycline for Chlamydia and metronidazole for anaerobes, started empirically because delay causes tubal damage and cultures are often negative.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Genital infections, PID & STIs in women
questions.stem: A painless indurated genital ulcer with rubbery non-tender inguinal nodes is characteristic of:
questions.concept: The syphilitic chancre is single, painless, indurated with a clean base and firm rubbery painless lymphadenopathy. Chancroid gives multiple painful ragged ulcers with tender suppurative nodes, and herpes multiple painful vesicles.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Genital infections, PID & STIs in women
questions.stem: Genital tuberculosis most commonly affects which part of the genital tract?
questions.concept: Haematogenous spread involves the fallopian tubes in 90 to 100% of genital tuberculosis, then the endometrium, and it is a leading cause of tubal infertility in India, often presenting with infertility, scanty menses or amenorrhoea.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Genital Tuberculosis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Genital infections, PID & STIs in women
questions.stem: The syndromic approach to sexually transmitted infection management is preferred at primary level because it:
options: Allows immediate treatment based on symptom clusters without laboratory facilities
Is cheaper than any other approach only
Eliminates the need for partner treatment
questions.concept: Syndromic management treats all likely pathogens for a presenting syndrome at the first visit using colour-coded kits, avoiding loss to follow-up where laboratories are unavailable, and includes partner treatment, condoms and counselling.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Genital infections, PID & STIs in women
questions.stem: Human papillomavirus types most associated with cervical carcinoma are:
questions.concept: HPV 16 and 18 cause about 70% of cervical cancers, while types 6 and 11 cause genital warts. The quadrivalent and nonavalent vaccines are most effective before sexual debut, at 9 to 14 years.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The most important support of the uterus preventing prolapse is:
questions.concept: The cardinal and uterosacral ligaments with the levator ani and endopelvic fascia provide the principal support. The round and broad ligaments contribute little, which is why their plication alone does not correct prolapse.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: A cystocele is a prolapse of the:
options: Anterior vaginal wall with the bladder
Posterior vaginal wall with the rectum
Pouch of Douglas with small bowel
questions.concept: Cystocele involves the anterior wall and bladder, rectocele the posterior wall and rectum, and enterocele the pouch of Douglas containing small bowel. The POP-Q system quantifies prolapse relative to the hymen.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The commonest cause of genitourinary fistula in India is:
options: Obstructed labour with prolonged pressure necrosis
questions.concept: Prolonged obstructed labour causes ischaemic pressure necrosis of the bladder base against the symphysis, producing vesicovaginal fistula - a disease of inadequate obstetric care. In developed countries, gynaecological surgery is the leading cause.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Genital Fistula

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Continuous involuntary urinary leakage with a normal urge to void suggests:
questions.concept: A fistula causes continuous leakage irrespective of position or effort, whereas stress incontinence leaks only on coughing or exertion and urge incontinence is preceded by a strong desire to void. Dye tests localise the fistula.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Genital Fistula

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The treatment of choice for stress urinary incontinence not responding to pelvic floor exercises is:
questions.concept: Mid-urethral tension-free tape restores urethral support and is the standard surgical treatment. Anticholinergics and beta-3 agonists treat overactive bladder with urge incontinence, not stress incontinence.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Overactive bladder with urge incontinence is best managed initially by:
options: Bladder training with an antimuscarinic or mirabegron
questions.concept: Behavioural bladder retraining with fluid and caffeine modification, plus an antimuscarinic such as solifenacin or the beta-3 agonist mirabegron, is first line. Intravesical botulinum toxin is reserved for refractory cases.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: A ring pessary is most appropriate for prolapse in a woman who:
options: Is unfit for surgery, pregnant or wishes to defer operation
questions.concept: A pessary provides mechanical support as a temporising or palliative measure in women unfit for or declining surgery, in pregnancy or in the puerperium, but requires periodic change and local oestrogen to prevent ulceration.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The Fothergill (Manchester) operation for prolapse involves:
options: Cervical amputation with plication of the cardinal ligaments and colporrhaphy
questions.concept: The Manchester operation amputates the elongated cervix and plicates the cardinal ligaments anterior to the cervical stump with anterior and posterior repair, conserving the uterus but often causing cervical stenosis and infertility.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Vault prolapse following hysterectomy is best treated by:
questions.concept: Sacrocolpopexy suspends the vault to the sacral promontory with mesh and has the best long-term durability; sacrospinous ligament fixation is the vaginal alternative. Prevention involves attaching the vault to the uterosacral ligaments at hysterectomy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Decubitus ulcer on a long-standing procidentia is caused by:
options: Venous congestion and friction of the dependent exposed vaginal mucosa
questions.concept: Chronic exposure with venous stasis produces a shallow ulcer that heals with rest, pessary and local oestrogen before surgery. Any indurated or non-healing ulcer requires biopsy to exclude carcinoma.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Menopause is diagnosed retrospectively after:
questions.concept: Menopause is the permanent cessation of menstruation confirmed after 12 months of amenorrhoea, occurring at a mean age of about 46 to 47 years in Indian women. Premature menopause is cessation before 40 years.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The hormonal profile of the postmenopausal woman shows:
options: High FSH and LH with low oestradiol
questions.concept: Loss of ovarian follicles removes negative feedback, so FSH rises markedly - more than LH because inhibin B also falls - while oestradiol falls. An FSH above 40 IU/L supports the diagnosis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The most effective treatment for troublesome vasomotor symptoms of menopause is:
options: Systemic oestrogen therapy, with a progestogen if the uterus is present
questions.concept: Systemic oestrogen is the most effective treatment for hot flushes and night sweats. A progestogen must be added in a woman with a uterus to prevent endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma from unopposed oestrogen.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The principal risk of unopposed oestrogen therapy in a woman with an intact uterus is:
questions.concept: Unopposed oestrogen causes endometrial proliferation, hyperplasia and eventually carcinoma, so cyclical or continuous progestogen is mandatory. After hysterectomy, oestrogen alone is appropriate.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Hormone therapy is contraindicated in a woman with:
options: A history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma or active thromboembolism
questions.concept: Absolute contraindications include hormone-dependent breast or endometrial cancer, active venous thromboembolism, active liver disease, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding and coronary or cerebrovascular disease.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Osteoporosis is defined by a bone mineral density T-score of:
questions.concept: WHO defines osteopenia as a T-score between minus 1 and minus 2.5 and osteoporosis as minus 2.5 or below on DEXA at the hip or lumbar spine. A fragility fracture establishes clinical osteoporosis irrespective of the score.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The first-line pharmacological treatment of postmenopausal osteoporosis is:
options: A bisphosphonate with calcium and vitamin D
questions.concept: Bisphosphonates such as alendronate or zoledronate inhibit osteoclastic resorption and reduce vertebral and hip fracture risk, given with adequate calcium and vitamin D. Oral bisphosphonates must be taken upright and fasting to avoid oesophagitis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: The most feared adverse effect of prolonged bisphosphonate therapy is:
options: Osteonecrosis of the jaw and atypical femoral fracture
questions.concept: Long-term suppression of bone turnover can cause osteonecrosis of the jaw, especially after dental extraction, and atypical subtrochanteric femoral fractures, prompting consideration of a drug holiday after 3 to 5 years.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Raloxifene, a selective oestrogen receptor modulator, acts as:
options: An agonist on bone with antagonist action on breast and endometrium
An agonist at all oestrogen receptors
questions.concept: Raloxifene preserves bone density and reduces vertebral fracture and breast cancer risk while not stimulating the endometrium, but it worsens hot flushes and increases thromboembolic risk.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.stem: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause with dyspareunia is best treated by:
questions.concept: Local vaginal oestrogen restores epithelial thickness, vascularity and pH with minimal systemic absorption, making it suitable even when systemic therapy is undesirable. Non-hormonal moisturisers are an alternative.
